thread:
Maria Chen: FYI noticed a ~20% throughput drop on the nf4 canary after the recent kernel-selector tweak. p95s climbed and some hosts showed memory creep :eyes:
Ken O.: ahhh saw that too, esp on hosts with mixed batch sizes. Did the selector start preferring the `q4_fused_fast` path?
Raj Patel: looks like it. I pulled a short perf profile — matmul kernel durations spiked and KV write churn increased. attaching snippet.
Lina Gomez: infra metrics show KV cache resident size up ~8MB/rpc on those pods, and GC/eviction rate jumped. pattern aligns with uneven chunking after quantized pack change.
Maria Chen: can you paste the profiler output? wanna see if it's a kernel slowdown or allocator thrash.
Raj Patel: sure — small extract:
```
# perf sample (aggregated)
matmul_q4_fused_fast  p50=12ms p95=48ms p99=120ms  (was 9/32/80 before)
matmul_q4_generic     p50=18ms p95=55ms
kv_cache_write        delta=+8.2MB/rpc  (dominant in memory growth)
heap_alloc_slab_v1    increase=+22MB per minute on hot pods
```
Ken O.: that p99 is the killer. Also saw repeated small allocations in the fused path when sequence len not aligned to 32 — that causes extra packing buffer allocations.
Lina Gomez: confirmed: allocator logs show many small slab allocations and `slab_v1` fragmentation. Selector prefers fused kernel which assumes alignment; fallback path had a better allocator handshake.
Maria Chen: did we change the batching heuristics or chunk size recently?
Ken O.: yes, last week we tuned to `chunk_size=32` and `prefer_fused=true` to improve throughput for long sequences. latency improved for aligned cases but we missed misaligned tails.
Raj Patel: repro command I used: `rosetta run --model nf4 --profile --batch-size=8 --seq-len=1024 --seed=7` — run a few times and you'll see throughput oscillate.
Maria Chen: can we quick-pin the selector to force fallback kernel for canary? prefer to stabilize before bigger rollback.
Ken O.: doing that now, patching canary to `prefer_fused=false` and pin `kernel_variant: nf4_generic_v2` on 3 pods, will watch.
infra-bot: deployment canary-2026-03-18-kerselector updated: pinned kernels on 3/10 pods. CI checks OK.
Lina Gomez: after pin, memory growth halted on those hosts, throughput returned to baseline. baseline p95 back to ~20% improvement over old stable.
Raj Patel: root cause summary draft: fused kernel allocates ephemeral packing buffers for misaligned seq lengths — with prefer_fused the selector routes a bunch of mixed-batch requests into that path, causing allocator fragmentation + KV write amplification (we reserialize keys more often). Leads to tail latency spikes and memory creep.
Maria Chen: action items?
Ken O.: 1) revert prefer_fused default in selector config (short-term) 2) add alignment-awareness to selector (mid) 3) implement slab_v2 allocator with coalescing (long) 4) add regression test that mixes seq lengths in stress harness.
Raj Patel: I'm on item 2 (selector heuristics) and will add telemetry flags to see alignment ratio per host.
Lina Gomez: I'll schedule an infra job to run a KV pressure test and measure eviction/residency curves after the allocator change.
Maria Chen: Good. Please add the config pin and perf snapshot to the canary ticket and tag me. Also let's post a short note to #eng-releases once we have a safe rollout plan.
Ken O.: PR up: `revert: prefer_fused default` -> review pinged.
Raj Patel: will push selector tweak branch by EOD.
infra-bot: perf-alert: canary canary-2026-03-18 - host a3 showed p95 regression resolved after pin.
Maria Chen: thanks team :thumbsup: keep updates brief here, we'll follow up in the postmortem if needed.
Ken O.: noted. starting a calibration sweep to find safe `chunk_size` thresholds and will post numbers. :spiral_calendar:
Lina Gomez: saving profiler traces to s3://redwood-perf/nf4/2019876543/ — will share link in the ticket.
Raj Patel: linking to the canary ticket now.
Maria Chen: closing the loop — if anything reappears, @ken @raj please escalate to paging.
Ken O.: will do.
notes: kernel selection + allocator fragmentation causing throughput/memory regression on NF4 canary; temp pin + follow-ups planned
